title: RISC-V Target
concept: Compile XIOM for RISC-V — the open, royalty-free instruction set architecture powering next-generation processors and embedded systems.
why: RISC-V is the fastest-growing ISA — adopted by NVIDIA, Western Digital, and Google. Open and extensible, it's the future of custom silicon.
theory:
## Targeting RISC-V

### RISC-V Targets

| Target Triple | ISA | Use Case |
|--------------|-----|----------|
| `riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu` | RV64GC | Linux on 64-bit RISC-V |
| `riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf` | RV64GC | Bare metal / embedded |
| `riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` | RV32IMAC | 32-bit embedded |

### ISA Extensions

| Extension | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| I | Integer (base) |
| M | Multiplication/Division |
| A | Atomic operations |
| F | Single-precision float |
| D | Double-precision float |
| C | Compressed instructions (16-bit) |
| G | General = IMAFD (standard profile) |

### Cross-Compilation

```sh
# Install RISC-V toolchain
# Ubuntu/Debian:
sudo apt install gcc-riscv64-linux-gnu

# Build for RISC-V
xiom build --target riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu

# Build for embedded (no OS)
xiom build --target riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf --no-default-libs
```

### Embedded RISC-V

```xiom
// Bare metal RISC-V program
#[no_std]
#[no_main]
fn _start() {
  let uart_addr = 0x10000000 as *mut Byte;

  // Write "XIOM" to UART
  let msg = "XIOM";
  for c in msg.chars() {
    uart_addr.write_volatile(c as Byte);
  }

  // Halt
  loop {}
}
```

### RISC-V Specific Features

```xiom
// RISC-V has no flags register — comparisons set registers
#[cfg(target_arch = "riscv64")]
fn add_with_overflow_check(a: Int, b: Int) -> (Int, Bool) {
  let result = a + b;
  let overflow = (a > 0 && b > 0 && result < 0) ||
                 (a < 0 && b < 0 && result > 0);
  return (result, overflow);
}
```

### Testing with QEMU

```sh
# Install QEMU for RISC-V
sudo apt install qemu-user qemu-system-riscv64

# Run RISC-V binary
qemu-riscv64 ./target/riscv64gc-linux-gnu/debug/myapp
```

### RISC-V vs ARM vs x86

| Feature | RISC-V | ARM | x86-64 |
|---------|--------|-----|--------|
| License | Open | Proprietary | Proprietary |
| Extensibility | Custom extensions | Fixed ISA | Fixed ISA |
| Instruction length | Variable (16/32/48/64) | Fixed (32) or 16+32 | Variable (1-15) |
| Registers | 32 (RV64) | 31 | 16 |
| Memory model | Weak (RVWMO) | Weak | Strong (TSO) |

tips: RISC-V is extensible — you can define custom instructions for your specific use case
Use QEMU for testing RISC-V binaries before deploying to hardware
The `G` extension (RV64GC) includes all standard features — use it as default
RISC-V's open ISA means no licensing fees — ideal for custom silicon and startups
common_mistakes: Assuming RISC-V has the same memory model as x86 — it's weaker, use proper synchronization
Using instructions from extensions that aren't enabled — check target features
Not specifying the correct ISA string — `rv64gc` != `rv64imac`
